text: A job fails. Should it try again right away?
Here is one job that sends an email, and the mail server is down.
After the first failure, it waits two seconds. After the second, four. Each time, the wait doubles: two to the power of the attempt.
But a hundred jobs failed at the same moment. If they all wait the same time, they all hit the server together again.
So each wait gets a small random extra, called jitter. The jobs spread out instead of arriving at once.
After twenty attempts, the runner stops trying.
The job moves to a state called discarded. It stays there for an engineer to look at, and never runs again on its own.
Wait longer each time, spread the crowd out, and know when to give up.
